title: Digital Twin-Based Smart Manufacturing: Dynamic Line Reconfiguration for Disturbance Handling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
reason: Here "agents" are physical resource options in an ontology, and a centralized optimizer makes the decisions. The paper proposes a general reconfiguration framework in which a process DT monitors disturbances and triggers reconfiguration, so the DT interfaces with decision-making.

title: Adaptive task planning and coordination in multi-agent manufacturing systems using large language models
reason: LLM-enabled multi-agent manufacturing control framework; product agent dynamically retrieves knowledge to handle unforeseen requirements beyond predefined capabilities, task planning and coordination, validated on an assembly testbed.

title: Dynamic distributed decision-making for resilient resource reallocation in disrupted manufacturing systems
reason: Proposes a model-based resource agent architecture and multi-agent coordination strategy for dynamic rescheduling after machine breakdowns, validated in simulation; no learning or DT integration evident, so I4 architecture/mechanism.

title: Agents enabling cyber-physical production systems
reason: Discusses agents as enabling technology for CPPS and demonstrates agent applicability in three production use cases with real-time/dependability requirements; agent-based manufacturing control architecture, not purely a survey.

title: Cyber-physical production systems architecture based on multi-agent’s design pattern—comparison of selected approaches mapping four agent patterns
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
reason: The paper compares MAS design patterns, but its stated main contribution is a CPPS architecture based on multi-agent patterns for manufacturing control, aligned with RAMI 4.0. That makes it an agent architecture paper rather than just a review.

title: A Framework for Automatic Initialization of Multi-Agent Production Systems Using Semantic Web Technologies
reason: Proposes framework initializing resource and product agents with semantic-web knowledge bases; PAs negotiate production sequences with RAs and handle failures—agent architecture and knowledge representation for manufacturing control.

title: Decentralized and on-the-fly agent-based service reconfiguration in manufacturing systems
reason: Proposes a decentralized agent-based approach where agents proactively find reconfiguration opportunities and reconfigure manufacturing services on the fly. Validated on a flexible manufacturing system case study. No learning or DT integration is described.

title: CASOA: An Architecture for Agent-Based Manufacturing System in the Context of Industry 4.0
reason: Proposes a cloud-assisted self-organized multi-agent architecture where smart agents negotiate, use ontological knowledge bases, and dynamically reconfigure for multi-product manufacturing. The overview section does not make it a review.

title: Priced Timed Automata Models for Control of Intelligent Product Agents in Manufacturing Systems
reason: Product agents in multi-agent manufacturing control use a priced timed automata environment model (a knowledge representation) to make production decisions. Shown in a semiconductor manufacturing simulation. No learning described.

title: Cooperative Product Agents to Improve Manufacturing System Flexibility: A Model-Based Decision Framework
reason: The paper proposes a cooperation framework in which product agents control individual parts and negotiate scheduling constraints with other agents. Decisions use a priced timed automata model and optimization, tested in simulation. No learning or DT use is described, so I4 rather than I1/I2.

title: Customization and flexible manufacturing capacity using a graphical method applied on a configurable multi-agent system
reason: Proposes a Plug & Produce goal-oriented configurable multi-agent system with a new part-agent strategy. Resources can be added or removed to balance capacity, and it was validated on a physical robot workstation for prefabricated wooden house production.

title: Automation platform independent multi-agent system for robust networks of production resources in industry 4.0
reason: Proposes a MAS concept for production resources, connected through OPC UA, that supports order-controlled production and adaptable factory reconfiguration. It is evaluated in use cases. This is an agent architecture for manufacturing control, with no learning or DT component described.

title: A CPPS-architecture and workflow for bringing agent-based technologies as a form of artificial intelligence into practice
reason: Presents MARIANNE, a multi-agent architecture of industrial agents for flexible Cyber-Physical Production Systems. It is aligned with I4.0 standards, uses design patterns and comes with an implementation guideline, so it counts as an agent architecture for manufacturing control.

title: Leveraging the Asset Administration Shell for Agent-Based Production Systems
reason: Proposes using digital twins (the Asset Administration Shell) to create agent-based production systems and their knowledge bases, so it fits the case of agents generated from DT models.

title: An intelligent manufacturing system based on a recursive control structure
reason: Proposes an immune-inspired framework network for multi-agent manufacturing systems with a recursive control structure. It handles disturbances such as machine failures and does scheduling (completion time, equipment load), so the agents make operational control decisions.

title: Integrating Human Operators into Agent-based Manufacturing Systems: A Table-top Demonstration
reason: Proposes a Human Resource Agent architecture integrated into multi-agent control with resource and product agents, demonstrated on a table-top manufacturing testbed; no learning or DT described.

title: Design and Implementation of a Smart, Product-Led Production Control Using Industrial Agents
venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Industrial Electronics
reason: Presents a multi-agent system used for product-led production control in a CPPS. It is built in an industrial agent framework and validated on an industrial lot-size-one filling process. No learning or DT integration is described.

title: Multi-agent system architectures for collaborative prognostics
reason: Compares multi-agent architectures in which industrial machines act as agents. The agents communicate, learn collaboratively to predict failures and optimise maintenance across fleets of industrial assets. These are learning agents making failure-handling decisions.

title: Describing Structure and Complex Interactions in Multi-Agent-Based Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
reason: Proposes a meta-model for structure and interactions in multi-agent industrial CPS for discrete production, covering dynamic decision making, delegation, resource reallocation, and rescheduling. This is an agent architecture/mechanism for manufacturing control.

title: Agent-Based Decentralized Manufacturing Execution System via Employment Network Collaboration
reason: Decentralized MES with WIPAgents, processing-resource agents and material-handling agents that collaborate through partner selection and data sharing. The digital twin is only the simulation testbed for validation, so this is not clear agent–DT integration.

title: Safe and efficient multi-agent planning for human–integrated smart manufacturing
reason: Multi-agent planning with agent ontology and runtime negotiation among agents to exclude unsafe skill edges in a Plug & Produce reconfigurable manufacturing system; it improves throughput. This is an agent mechanism for production control.

title: Safe and reconfigurable manufacturing: safety aware multi-agent control for Plug & Produce system
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
reason: Proposes multi-agent control for Plug & Produce manufacturing in which agents reason about task allocations to avoid safety risks during operation and reconfiguration. This is an agent mechanism for manufacturing control; no learning or DT is described.

title: Design, Application, and Evaluation of a Multiagent System in the Logistics Domain
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
reason: Agent-based control for automated material flow systems within production systems: module agents with knowledge bases, communication ontology, decentralized routing and runtime reconfiguration, validated in simulation and a lab demonstrator. No learning agents described.

title: Finite-Time Consensus and Readjustment Three-Stage Filter for Predictive Schedules in FMS
reason: Proposes a distributed MAS for FMS where agents cooperate to execute production tasks via event-based consensus control and ROS message exchange, avoiding deadlocks; validated on a physical factory simulation platform.

title: An Intelligent Framework for Multi-Agent System Based on Dynamic Balancing of Production 4.0
reason: MAS framework where agents represent workstations, operators, equipment and negotiate task assignment for dynamic assembly line rebalancing; operational decisions with productivity/OEE results. No clear learning or DT component.

title: Cloud-based multi-agent architecture for effective planning and scheduling of distributed manufacturing
reason: Proposes a cloud-based multi-agent architecture for distributed manufacturing. Autonomous agents interact to fix internal discrepancies and handle order variations in planning and scheduling. Demonstrated in a simulated case study.

title: Autonomous production control for matrix production based on deep Q-learning
reason: The paper uses deep Q-learning for production control in matrix production, with independent coordinating agents that allocate orders and production steps to machines. It reports throughput time, so these are learning agents making operational decisions.

title: Agent Cooperation Mechanism for Decentralized Manufacturing Scheduling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Man and Cybernetics Systems
reason: Proposes an agent cooperation mechanism: manufacturer agents negotiate and cooperate to schedule operations (MT10 job-shop data) in decentralized manufacturing scheduling. Agents make operational scheduling decisions, so this is not just analytical simulation.

title: Digital Twin Based SUDIHA Architecture to Smart Shopfloor Scheduling
venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
reason: Holonic architecture (Product, Resource, Order holons) for dynamic shopfloor scheduling handling disruptions, enhanced with Digital Twin configuration per holon; agents integrated with DTs, validated in a flexible workshop case study.

title: Artificial immune systems as a design pattern for disturbance management in cyber-physical production systems
reason: Proposes an immune-inspired, product-driven distributed control architecture for CPPS. Embedded product agents detect, evaluate and react to disturbances on their own (case retrieval, coordination). Validated in a multi-agent learning factory simulation.

title: Reducing Nervousness in Master Production Planning: A Systematic Approach Incorporating Product-Driven Strategies
reason: Proposes a product-driven system in which intelligent agents make production decisions, changing forecasted production quantities each period in master production planning. These are product agents making operational decisions; no learning or DT is described.

title: A product-driven system approach to generate fast solutions to the job shop scheduling problem.
reason: Agents represent intelligent products in a product-driven system and make distributed scheduling decisions for the job shop. They use a shifting bottleneck heuristic, not learning, so I4 applies rather than I1.

title: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response for discrete manufacturing systems energy management
reason: Multi-agent deep RL (MADDPG) produces machine schedules for a discrete battery assembly manufacturing system, keeping production tasks while cutting energy cost. Learning agents make operational scheduling decisions for machines.

title: Optimized Adaptive Scheduling of a Manufacturing Process System with Multi-skill Workforce and Multiple Machine Types: An Ontology-based, Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
reason: Proposes an ontology-based multi-agent reinforcement learning approach for adaptive flow-shop scheduling, with workforce and machines cooperating in real time. These are learning agents making operational scheduling decisions.

title: A multi-agent framework for capability-based reconfiguration of industrial assembly systems
reason: Multi-agent framework for reconfiguring industrial assembly systems: plug-in/out resources, dynamic capability aggregation, implemented on an industrial assembly system. No learning or DT described, so it falls under agent architecture.

title: Digital Twin Shop-Floor: A New Shop-Floor Paradigm Towards Smart Manufacturing
reason: Proposes a digital twin shop-floor concept with four key components plus operation mechanisms. That is a DT framework for a manufacturing system with no agents, and its service system links the DT to control and management.

title: Digital Twin Data Modeling with AutomationML and a Communication Methodology for Data Exchange
reason: No agents. Proposes a general AutomationML-based DT data modeling and communication methodology for data exchange between systems connected to the DT. This addresses standards alignment and DT interfacing in manufacturing.

title: FMU-supported simulation for CPS Digital Twin
reason: No agents. Proposes a general modular DT simulation architecture for production systems, built on a semantic data model and FMU-based standard interfaces, to support decision makers. This addresses standards alignment and the DT–decision interface.

title: Digital twin-based WEEE recycling, recovery and remanufacturing in the background of Industry 4.0
reason: No agents. Proposes a novel digital twin-based system for WEEE remanufacturing operations with international standard-compliant data models, which is a DT framework aligned with standards.

title: A Reconfigurable Modeling Approach for Digital Twin-based Manufacturing System
reason: No agents. Proposes a five-dimensional DT modeling approach for manufacturing systems, with expandable model structure and reserved interfaces to objective functions and optimization algorithms, i.e., how DTs interface with decision-making components.

title: A framework for manufacturing system reconfiguration and optimisation utilising digital twins and modular artificial intelligence
reason: No agents described. Proposes a general framework combining digital twins with modular AI for system-level reconfiguration decisions. It addresses how DTs interface with decision-making through a data pipeline and API, applied to manufacturing.

title: Open Process Automation- and Digital Twin-Based Performance Monitoring of a Process Manufacturing System
reason: No agents. Proposes a DT framework for monitoring process manufacturing performance, built on the Open Process Automation reference architecture (standards alignment/interoperability), with guidelines for developing system-wide DT solutions.

title: Digital Twin Service towards Smart Manufacturing
reason: No agents. The paper specifies how digital twin components are provided to manufacturers as services, and how the DT links to manufacturing planning and production control. That counts as a DT framework and touches how DTs interface with decision-making.

title: Integrating the Digital Twin of the manufacturing system into a decision support system for improving the order management process
reason: No agents mentioned. Proposes a conceptual framework that integrates the manufacturing system's Digital Twin into a decision support system for order management, addressing how the DT interfaces with decision-making.

title: A concept in synchronization of virtual production system with real factory based on anchor-point method
reason: No agents. The paper presents the structure of a Digital Twin for production plants and a general anchor-point method that keeps cross-domain DT data models in sync with the real system, which addresses DT characteristics.

title: An approach for leveraging Digital Twins in agent-based production systems
reason: Multi-agent system for decentralized production in which agents are initialized from Digital Twins (Asset Administration Shell) via a parser. These are agents generated from DT models, which matches I2.

title: BIOSOARM: a bio-inspired self-organising architecture for manufacturing cyber-physical shopfloors
reason: Proposes a reference architecture where shopfloor components and product parts are autonomous decoupled entities that interact and cooperate to self-organise production flows; tested in flow-line and job-shop scenarios.

title: The Digital Twin: Realizing the Cyber-Physical Production System for Industry 4.0
reason: No agents. Proposes a general DT concept for production systems: multimodal data acquisition requirements, database composition, and implementation guidelines for SMEs. DT is coupled to the physical system as a basis for optimization (decision interface).

title: Integration of digital twin and deep learning in cyber‐physical systems: towards smart manufacturing
reason: No agents; proposes a reference architecture combining DT, deep learning and 5C-CPS for manufacturing, providing predictive services and actionable insights, which suggests a DT framework interfacing with decision-making.

title: Framework for a digital twin in manufacturing: Scope and requirements
reason: No agents. Sets out key DT characteristics, scope and requirements for manufacturing, and ties them to the ISO 23247 standard. That covers the DT characteristics and standards-alignment conditions, though it partly synthesizes earlier perspectives.

title: Development of a multidimensional conceptual model for job shop smart manufacturing scheduling from the Industry 4.0 perspective
reason: The paper starts from a literature review but contributes its own conceptual framework for job shop scheduling. That framework combines a hierarchical agent structure with deep reinforcement learning to support rescheduling and autonomous operation, so the agents are learning agents.

title: Architecture and knowledge modelling for self-organized reconfiguration management of cyber-physical production systems
venue: International Journal of Computer Integrated Manufacturing
reason: Presents a novel multi-agent system with MAPE-K for self-organized reconfiguration management of cyber-physical production systems, with knowledge modelling via a UML information model: an agent architecture applied to manufacturing reconfiguration.

title: Local Decision Making based on Distributed Digital Twin Framework
reason: No agents described. Proposes a distributed DT framework for manufacturing with a decision-making module that notifies the MES to trigger reconfiguration and scheduling, addressing the DT interface with decision-making. Evaluated on a pilot line.

title: An Adaptive Real-Time Scheduling Method for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem With Combined Processing Constraint
reason: Multi-agent system for flexible job shop scheduling in which each job agent uses contextual bandit learning to pick its dispatching rule based on the environment state. These are learning agents making operational scheduling decisions.

title: Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems Characteristics in Digital Twin Context
reason: No agents. Introduces a DT-RMS concept, a cyber-replica framework for reconfigurable manufacturing that covers the required RMS characteristics and supports reconfiguration decisions at design and operating time.

title: Anarchic manufacturing: Distributed control for product transition
reason: Free-market distributed planning and control system: job and machine agents make decisions autonomously and cooperate through dynamic batching and changeover profitability assessments. Evaluated in manufacturing product transition, including an automotive case study.

title: A data- and knowledge-driven framework for digital twin manufacturing cell
reason: Proposes a data- and knowledge-driven DT framework for manufacturing cells, with key enabling technologies and DT support for perceiving, predicting, optimizing and controlling. No agents are described, so it falls in the DT framework supporting set.

title: Cognitive Digital Twin for industrial maintenance: operational framework for fault detection and diagnosis
reason: No agents; proposes a general Cognitive DT framework for manufacturing maintenance with ontology and cognitive capabilities, and defines how the CDT's output feeds the maintenance decision-making process (DT interface with decision-making). Includes review part but contributes its own framework.

title: Increasing Interoperability between Digital Twin Standards and Specifications: Transformation of DTDL to AAS
reason: No agents. Proposes a generic mapping between DT specifications (DTDL to Asset Administration Shell) for Industry 4.0 interoperability. This is a DT specification contribution that addresses alignment with standards, and it was tested on a physical asset.

title: Methodology and Tools for Digital Twin Management—The FA3ST Approach
reason: No agents. The paper proposes a DT lifecycle model and a methodology for DT management, aligned with standards such as the Asset Administration Shell, OPC UA, AML and IDS, for industrial assets.

title: Semantic Microservice Framework for Digital Twins
reason: No agents. The paper proposes a general DT service framework architecture for industrial cyber-physical systems, built from identified requirements, using Semantic Web technology and workflow orchestration. A proof of concept on an industrial process is shown.

title: XRTwin4Industry: Empowering industrial digital twins with XR and instruction system - a framework for standardization and interoperability
reason: Proposes a standard-oriented XR-enabled DT framework for industrial settings that is aligned with the Asset Administration Shell and addresses interoperability. It is applied to a robotic arm and an assembly line. No agents are described.

title: A Reusable and Maintainable Digital Twin Framework for State Estimation Using Physics-Based Models of Mechanical Systems: Predictive Maintenance Case Studies
reason: No agents. The paper proposes a general DT framework for state estimation in smart manufacturing. It addresses required DT characteristics (maintainability, reusability) and gives high-confidence estimations, which counts as uncertainty-related output.

title: Evolvable Operational Digital Twin Architecture for Real-Time Field-Level Control of Distributed, Adaptable, and Self-Organizing Manufacturing Systems
reason: The paper proposes a DT architecture that integrates multi-agent systems and skill-based control. The DT is used at runtime for fault handling and task scheduling in a self-organizing manufacturing system, which counts as agent–DT integration.

title: Real-time order dispatching for a fleet of autonomous mobile robots using multi-agent reinforcement learning
reason: The abstract proposes multi-agent RL in which each AMR is an agent that learns to bid on transport orders in a production environment. That is learning agents representing transporters and making operational dispatching decisions.

title: Application of a Simulation-Based Digital Twin for Predicting Distributed Manufacturing Control System Performance
reason: Proposes an architecture integrating an agent-based distributed manufacturing control system with its simulation-based DT to predict runtime performance; agent–DT integration in shop-floor control.

title: Spillover Algorithm: A decentralised coordination approach for multi-robot production planning in open shared factories
reason: Proposes a decentralized multi-agent coordination algorithm in which self-interested robot owners and item owners act as agents and decide robot allocation and production planning in shared factories.

title: Multi-Agent Modeling of Cyber-Physical Systems for IEC 61499 Based Distributed Automation
reason: Proposes two-layer architecture: multi-agent model (SPADE) for high-level intelligence over IEC 61499 distributed industrial automation control, tested on hardware; agents communicate and control physical modules.

title: An integrated data- and capability-driven approach to the reconfiguration of agent-based production systems
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
reason: Multi-agent system handles reconfiguration of distributed production resources, matching capabilities to product requirements, with a machine learning self-adaptation technique that learns from past adjustments; evaluated on a robotic manufacturing system.

title: An Agent-Based System for Automated Configuration and Coordination of Robotic Operations in Real Time—A Case Study on a Car Floor Welding Process
venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
reason: Agent-based framework with ontology knowledge models where production automation agents configure, control and coordinate robotic operations; resources embed themselves autonomously. Validated in a lab robotic assembly cell using car-floor welding data.

title: DIGITAL TWIN: MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE THROUGH VIRTUAL FACTORY REPLICATION
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
reason: No agents. Proposes a DT concept for injection molding: a DT for each stage, integrated into one model, with required data and technologies and bidirectional control that supports responsive decisions. This counts as a framework that addresses DT characteristics and the decision interface.

title: Digital twins of human robot collaboration in a production setting
reason: No agents. Proposes a digital twin framework for design, build and control of human-robot collaborative assembly, continuously mirroring the physical system. The control role suggests a DT interface with decision-making; validated at a manufacturing company.

title: A Feature-Based Framework for Structuring Industrial Digital Twins
reason: No agents. Proposes a feature-based DT framework (FDTF) for industrial digital twins that defines and structures DTs by common features, which counts as required/optional DT characteristics. Title indicates an industrial context.

title: Application of IoT-Aided Simulation to Manufacturing Systems in Cyber-Physical System
reason: No agents; proposes a general DT construction framework and IoT data-input scheme for manufacturing systems, discussing important issues (characteristics) in DT development, verified with a DT-oriented simulation model.

title: Digital twin and the asset administration shell
reason: No agents. Pulls shared digital twin requirements (characteristics) from existing DT definitions and maps them to the three Asset Administration Shell types, which addresses DT characteristics and alignment with the AAS standard.

title: Use of Asset Administration Shell Coupled with ISO 15926 to Facilitate the Exchange of Equipment Condition and Health Status Data of a Process Plant
reason: No agents. Proposes an AAS-based digital representation specification (a neutral format and data structure) for process plant equipment, aligned with the AAS and ISO 15926 standards. This fits a DT framework/specification with standards alignment.

title: Asset administration shell submodel for wireless communication system.
reason: No agents are described. The paper proposes an Asset Administration Shell (DT) submodel specification for communication systems in Industry 4.0 production. That aligns with the AAS standard and supports negotiation with the production system.

title: Decentralized Skill-based Control Concept for Adaptable Production Plants
reason: Autonomous modules offer skills via AAS interfaces. They decide the material flow of workpieces and talk to each other through an AAS Agent Server. This is a decentralized control architecture, tested in simulation and on a real model factory.

title: Asset Administration Shell for PLC Representation Based on IEC 61131–3
reason: No agents. Proposes a standards-aligned Asset Administration Shell model, i.e. a digital representation specification for manufacturing assets, covering IEC 61131-3 programs, PLCs and plant devices. This fits D1's requirement of alignment with standards.

title: Clarifying concepts of Metaverse, Digital Twin, Digital Thread and AAS for CPS-based production systems
reason: Not agent-based. It uses a literature study but contributes its own hierarchical view clarifying DT definitions and how DTs relate to the Asset Administration Shell standard in CPS-based production systems, so it counts as a DT framework contribution.

title: Digital Twin Reference Model Development to Prevent Operators’ Risk in Process Plants
reason: No agents. Proposes a layered DT reference model for process plants (physical space, communication, DT, user space). It covers standardization issues and how DTs support corrective-action decisions.

title: MES-integrated digital twin frameworks
reason: No agents described. Proposes MES-integrated DT frameworks, distinguishing DT from digital shadow, with an intelligence layer for decision making (error states, disassembly triggering); addresses DT characteristics and DT–decision interface, validated in lab.

title: A generic tri-model-based approach for product-level digital twin development in a smart manufacturing environment
reason: No agents. The paper proposes a generic CPS architecture and a tri-model approach (digital, computational, graph-based models) for building product-level DTs in smart manufacturing. It addresses DT reference models and characteristics, which is a DT framework contribution.

title: A Digital Twin-based scheduling framework including Equipment Health Index and Genetic Algorithms
reason: No agents. Proposes a DT-based scheduling framework and architecture in which a DT simulator with an Equipment Health Indicator module feeds a genetic-algorithm scheduler, which covers how DTs interface with decision-making. Validated on a lab assembly line.

title: 5-Dimensional Definition for a Manufacturing Digital Twin
reason: Proposes a general five-layer manufacturing DT model combining a 5-Dimensional DT definition and cloud-based CPS architecture. Its analysis layer supports decision-making and reconfiguration, so it covers how DTs interface with decision-making. No agents.

title: The MAS4AI framework for human-centered agile and smart manufacturing
reason: Proposes a MAS in which software agents cooperate with workers for dynamic, reconfigurable production. AAS submodels act as the integration layer and enable self-configuration and plug-and-produce. This is an AAS-based agent architecture for manufacturing control.

title: Design and Installation of an Agent-Controlled Cyber-Physical Production System Using the Example of a Beverage Bottling Plant
venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Industrial Electronics
reason: Presents a beverage bottling CPPS built from industrial resources and controlled by a multiagent system, with an evaluation on two use cases. This fits an agent architecture applied to manufacturing control.

title: Towards Sustainable Cyber-Physical Manufacturing Systems
reason: Proposes a self-managing services architecture using software agents and IEC 61499 function blocks that reconfigure part routings when equipment fails. This is a manufacturing control agent architecture, tested in simulation.

title: ONTOLOGY AS A TOOL FOR CREATING OPEN MULTI-AGENT RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS
reason: Proposes ontology-based multi-agent resource planning with an enterprise knowledge base, new agent classes for demand-resource networks, and a multi-agent planning method that can be customized to specific manufacturing areas.

title: Application of the Multi-Agent Platform for Development of Smart Resource Management Systems in Real-Time
reason: The paper proposes a multi-agent demand-resource network platform. Order and resource agents negotiate compromises to plan and replan production resources in real time. It was deployed for workshop management at a machine-building enterprise, so manufacturing operations are covered.

title: Digital twin-based opti-state control method for a synchronized production operation system
reason: No agents. Proposes a digital twin-based control framework (DTCF) for a production system. The framework supplies full element information to the opti-state control decision-making in a virtual control layer, which covers the DT–decision interface.

title: Towards an ontology-based dictionary for production planning and control in the domain of injection molding as a basis for standardized asset administration shells
reason: No agents described. Contributes an ontology/vocabulary specification as a foundation for standardized Asset Administration Shell digital twins in injection molding PPC, aligned with established standards.

title: RMPFQ: A Quality-Oriented Knowledge Modelling Method for Manufacturing Systems Towards Cognitive Digital Twins
reason: No agents. Proposes a semantic-driven DT architecture for manufacturing, formalized with an ontology that follows the IOF-Core and BFO ontology standards and is mapped to the Cognitive Digital Twin concept. Validated on a washing-machine assembly case.

title: Enabling a Multi-Agent System for Resilient Production Flow in Modular Production Systems
reason: Presents a MAS/holonic semi-heterarchical design for resilient production planning and execution in modular production. It uses Asset Administration Shells as agent interfaces and is evaluated in a simulated automotive production environment.

title: Decentralized Holonic Control System Model for Line-less Mobile Assembly Systems
reason: The paper reviews literature but presents its own decentralized holonic multi-agent control system, with role, interaction and data models, for configuring assembly stations in line-less mobile assembly systems.

title: Design model for digital shadows to support reconfiguration decisions in manufacturing
reason: No agents described. Proposes a design model for digital shadows (a DT-type framework) for reconfigurable manufacturing. Its information base feeds decision-support components (Time-expanded Decision Networks), so it addresses how DTs interface with decision-making.

title: Autonomous Agent-Based Adaptation of Energy-Optimized Production Schedules Using Extensive-Form Games
reason: Scheduler and energy agents play extensive-form games to adapt production schedules to energy price changes and production disturbances in modular CPPS. Validated in simulation and on a real-world demonstrator, so these are operational decision agents.

title: ML2MAS: a multi-agent reinforcement learning and BNNs-GAN integration framework for smart manufacturing optimization
reason: The paper proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which agents make decentralized, real-time predictive maintenance decisions in manufacturing. These are learning agents making operational decisions.

title: Self-configurable Manufacturing Industrial Agents (SMIA): a standardized approach for digitizing manufacturing assets
reason: FIPA-compliant industrial agents are generated automatically from AAS-based Digital Twin descriptions. They coordinate with peers, negotiate autonomously and carry out skills for manufacturing assets, validated in a robotic logistics scenario.

title: From Automation to Autonomy: A Digital Twin Framework for Transparent Agent and Human Collaboration in Industrial Multi-Agent Systems
reason: Proposes a framework for industrial multi-agent systems in which a DT infrastructure acts as a service layer for coordinating and supervising autonomous agents. It uses a standards-based data model and is evaluated in a real industrial case study.

title: Agent-Based Supervision for Service-Oriented Industrial Cyber–Physical Systems
reason: Industrial agents supervise and dynamically reconfigure service-oriented industrial CPS. They select services and monitor performance online, which are operational reconfiguration decisions. This is an agent architecture applied to industrial automation control.

title: Distributed Control of Collaborative Multi-Agent Systems using Interpreted Petri Nets through Indirect Interactions
reason: Proposes a distributed multi-agent control framework using Interpreted Petri nets. The agents work together to work out how to meet a shared specification, and it is demonstrated on a collaborative assembly system, which counts as manufacturing control.

title: Agentic Manufacturing Operations Management: Concept and First Prototype
reason: Proposes ISA-95-aligned agent layer where MOM activities (scheduling, dispatching, execution) are autonomous agents with a digital twin layer; prototype uses LLM-enabled agents executing and analysing experiments in battery production.

title: Agentic AI for decentralized, natural-language communication and interaction between agents in self-organizing manufacturing systems
reason: Presents an LLM-based multi-agent system for self-organizing manufacturing in which agents allocate tasks dynamically by communicating in natural language. Agents that query foundation models fall under I1, the highest-priority match.

title: AI Native Manufacturing Operating System for Autonomous Smart Factories Using Digital Twins, Multi Agent Artificial Intelligence, Physics Informed Machine Learning, and Reinforcement Learning.
reason: Every machine, robot, vehicle and station is represented as a negotiating agent in a market. An RL engine adapts that market, and the agents are integrated with a Digital Twin Kernel. These are learning agents making operational decisions in manufacturing.

title: LLM-Based Modelling of AAS-Compliant Digital Twins to Describe Capabilities in Manufacturing-as-a-Service
reason: No decision-making agents. The paper proposes an LLM-supported, ontology-based generation process and a modular architecture for AAS-compliant DTs describing manufacturing capabilities. This is a DT framework aligned with a standard (AAS).

title: Enhancing stability and robustness in online machine shop scheduling: A multi-agent system and negotiation-based approach for handling machine downtime in industry 4.0
reason: Multi-agent system in which machine agents negotiate job swaps for partial rescheduling during machine downtime. The machines also individually learn how to evaluate and adapt bids, so these are learning agents making operational decisions.

title: Self-optimization in distributed manufacturing systems using Modular State-based Stackelberg games
reason: Self-learning agents representing manufacturing modules make cooperative, hierarchical control decisions through game-theoretic learning. Tested on laboratory testbeds, with reduced overflow and lower power consumption reported.

title: Multicast dataset synchronization and agent negotiation in distributed manufacturing control systems
reason: Proposes a multi-agent manufacturing control architecture with multicast dataset synchronization and an agent negotiation mechanism for operation sequencing and resource allocation, implemented in JADE. No learning or DT component is described.

title: Integrating large language model and digital twins in the context of industry 5.0: Framework, challenges and opportunities
reason: Not just a review: proposes the Interactive-DT framework for integrating LLMs with DTs in manufacturing, with LLM roles at the edge, DT and service layers. No agents are described, so D1 (DT framework) applies.

title: Personas to inform cognitive interaction with a Digital Twin
reason: No agents. Proposes a human-centric DT definition and a requirements levels matrix for DT users, which addresses DT characteristics and how DTs interface with human decision-making. Demonstrated on an industrial gearbox in the manufacturing domain.

title: A study on deep reinforcement learning-based crane scheduling model for uncertainty tasks
reason: Deep RL multi-crane scheduling in a steelmaking workshop where each crane is the intelligent agent learning scheduling decisions; this matches learning agents that represent resources and make operational decisions.

title: A local industrial-agent middleware for resilient manufacturing execution systems under weak external connectivity
reason: Industrial agents built on Semantic Kernel with retrieval propose recovery actions that are executed through MES services for disruption handling on power-supply production lines. Querying a foundation model matches I1, the highest-priority ID.
